Title: MathUtils.gcd(Integer.MIN_VALUE, 0) should throw an Exception instead of returning Integer.MIN_VALUE

The gcd method should throw an Exception for gcd(Integer.MIN_VALUE, 0), like for gcd(Integer.MIN_VALUE, Integer.MIN_VALUE). The method should only return nonnegative results.

Bug report:
Title: MathUtils.gcd(Integer.MIN_VALUE, 0) should throw an Exception instead of returning Integer.MIN_VALUE

The gcd method should throw an Exception for gcd(Integer.MIN_VALUE, 0), like for gcd(Integer.MIN_VALUE, Integer.MIN_VALUE). The method should only return nonnegative results.

input.issue_gist: MathUtils.gcd(Integer.MIN_VALUE, 0) returns Integer.MIN_VALUE (a negative number) instead of throwing an ArithmeticException, since the true result 2^31 can't be represented as a nonnegative int. This is inconsistent with gcd(Integer.MIN_VALUE, Integer.MIN_VALUE), which already throws.

concrete_examples.expected: Throws an ArithmeticException (result 2^31 overflows int; gcd must be nonnegative)

concrete_examples.actual: Throws an ArithmeticException (correct; this is the reference behavior)
